## Learning about passivity from data

Alexandre Sanfelici Bazanella

Results on benchmark are presented to illustrate its properties, including its robustness to noise.  Various uses of the storage function that do not require knowledge of model are also discussed.

## INTRODUCTION

This is what this paper is about: in it, a purely data-driven methodology to obtain storage function is presented. The methodology consists in solving a linear optimization program (LP) formed with inputloutputlstate data collected from the system, without the need any priors. The LP yields the optimal parameter values of a dictionary parametrization of the storage function. A hyperparameter of the LP allows to make the solution robust to noise and to numerical errors. for

Passivity is fundamental property of dynamical systems that   plays major role in systems   and control   theory at least 1960sDetermining whether system is passive or not, and to which degree; revolves arounds finding an appropriate   function   describing its   energy dissipation properties the   storage function. Passivity concerns the input-output relation of the system; and yet a storage function can also be used as Lyapunov function, thus allowing to study the stability of the unforced behavior of the as well. Once various tasks can be performed using its knowledge: estimate the domain of attraction, estimate the convergence rate of autonomous trajectories, design controller to improve this convergence rate, certify previously designed controller; etc; this is all standard theory [6], [13]. What is much less recognized in the model-based tradition of systems and control theory is that these tasks require knowledge only of the storage function and not of the model. system

storage function for analytically   from its   model, but knowledge of model is by no means guarantee that storage function can be found. There are no general fail-proof methods for that; except  for  linear   systems. Known methods are   either   for restricted classes of systems [6], rely on nonrobust numerical procedures [8], [14], andlor are constructive design methods that actually passivate a given system through control, instead of verifying the passivity of the uncontrolled system [7], [13] So, from an applications perspective the relationship between models and storage functions is somewhat  problematic: on one hand, in a variety of applications the model serves only as means to find a storage function; becoming superfluous once it is found; but on the other hand the knowledge of a model is often not enough to find a useful storage function. Therefore, alternative ways of finding a storage function that do not rely on an analytical model are to be welcomed, even when such model is available. good Recently; research on data-driven control has experimented boost [1], [4] and considerable   amount of this   work involves Lyapunov analysis.  Among these works, the ones that deal with nonlinear systems usually consist of control synthesis [3] (as opposed to analysis), and rarely deal  with passivity  [9], [11] Also; the vast work treats   discrete-time systems, whereas   this paper is devoted to continuous time systems.

Results for classical benchmark the  pendulum are presented in Section IV. Various uses of the storage function are discussed in Section V Finally; lines of future and present  work are outlined in Section VI.
